Scenario: Valid standard user logs in
Steps:
1. Enter username and password
2. Click Login
Expected: Products page opens and lists 6 products
Actual: Products page opened, 6 products listed

Scenario: Catalogue shows name, price and a distinct image for every product
Steps:
1. Open the products page
2. Inspect each product tile
Expected: 6 tiles; each has a name, a price and its own product image (6 different image files)
Actual: 6 tiles, 6 distinct images

Scenario: Sort products by name Z to A
Steps:
1. Open the sort dropdown
2. Select "Name (Z to A)"
Expected: Products are listed in reverse alphabetical order
Actual: First product: "Test.allTheThings() T-Shirt (Red)"; last: "Sauce Labs Backpack"

Scenario: Sort products by price low to high
Steps: 1. Select "Price (low to high)"
Expected: Prices are in ascending numeric order

Scenario: Product detail page matches the product that was clicked
Steps:
1. Note name and price of the first product
2. Click its name
3. Compare detail page
Expected: Detail page shows the same name and price
Actual: Detail shows "Sauce Labs Backpack" $29.99

Scenario: Add three products to the cart
Pre-conditions: Logged in as standard_user, cart empty
Steps:
1. Click Add to cart on the first three products
2. Open the cart
Expected: Badge shows 3, buttons turn into Remove, cart lists the 3 products
Actual: Badge 3, 3 Remove buttons, 3 items in cart

Scenario: Remove a product from the cart page
Steps:
1. Open the cart
2. Click Remove on the first product
Expected: Product disappears from the cart and the badge drops to 1
Actual: 1 item left, badge 1

Scenario: Complete a purchase end to end
Steps:
1. Add one product
2. Open cart, Checkout
3. Enter first name, last name, postal code
4. Continue, then Finish
Expected: "Thank you for your order!" is shown and the cart badge is cleared
Actual: Header "Thank you for your order!", badge empty

Scenario: Logout ends the session
Steps:
1. Open menu, click Logout
2. Request /inventory.html directly
Expected: Login page shown; the direct request is refused with a "must be logged in" message
Actual: Message: Epic sadface: You can only access '/inventory.html' when you are logged in.

Scenario: Order overview totals: item total, 8% tax, grand total
Steps:
1. Add the first two products
2. Go through checkout to the overview
3. Compare item total, tax and total with the product prices
Test Data: standard_user; $29.99 + $9.99 (tax rate 8% is observed behaviour, rounded to cents)
Expected: Item total = sum of prices; tax = 8% rounded to 2 decimals; total = item total + tax
Actual: Item total $39.98, tax $3.2, total $43.18 (expected item total $39.98)

Scenario: Cart contents survive navigation to a detail page and back
Steps:
1. Add the first product
2. Open its detail page
3. Click Back to products
Expected: Badge still shows 1 and the product still offers Remove
Actual: Badge 1, 1 Remove button

Scenario: Cancel on checkout step one returns to the cart with items intact
Steps:
1. Open checkout step one
2. Click Cancel
Expected: Cart page opens and still lists the product
Actual: URL /cart.html, 1 item

Scenario: Reset App State empties the cart
Steps:
1. Open menu
2. Click Reset App State
Expected: Badge disappears and all buttons show Add to cart
Actual: Badge empty; 4 of 6 buttons show Add to cart, the rest still show Remove until reload. See F-04

Scenario: Protected page cannot be opened without logging in
Steps: 1. Open /inventory.html directly in a new browser context
Expected: Redirected to login with an "only access when logged in" message
Actual: Message: Epic sadface: You can only access '/inventory.html' when you are logged in.

Scenario: Checkout is not possible with an empty cart
Steps:
1. Open the cart
2. Click Checkout
3. Enter valid details and continue
Expected: Checkout is blocked or the user is told the cart is empty
Actual: Checkout step one opened; overview reached with 0 items (/checkout-step-two.html). See F-01

Scenario: Locked out user cannot log in
Steps:
1. Enter locked-out credentials
2. Click Login
Expected: Stays on login; message "Sorry, this user has been locked out."
Actual: Message: Epic sadface: Sorry, this user has been locked out.
